sections.h2: How quickly can a Pflugerville house be sold?
sections.html:
It depends on the route. A cash buyer can often close in a few weeks, while a listing usually takes longer because of showings, a buyer's inspection and loan approval. Pflugerville sits about fifteen miles north of Austin, so buyers here tend to compare it with Austin and Round Rock before they make an offer.

A cash sale trades some price for speed, fewer showings and a closing date you pick. A listing can bring more money but adds repairs, staging and a financing contingency. Weigh both with a written offer in hand.

  • Choose a direct sale when time pressure, repairs, tenants or a lien make a listing hard.
  • Choose a listing when the house is in good shape and you can wait for top price.
  • Read every closing cost line before you sign.

sections.h2: How did Pflugerville grow, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Pflugerville lies on Farm Road 1825 in northeastern Travis County. The Texas State Historical Association says it was named for Henry Pfluger, who brought his family from Germany in 1849, and that residents started a school in 1872 and a Lutheran church in 1875.

A post office opened in 1893 with Louis Bohls as postmaster. In the mid-1890s the community had about 250 people and did its banking and shipping in Round Rock, eight miles away. When the Missouri, Kansas and Texas line passed just outside town in 1904, the population doubled within ten years to 500.

After World War II people moved to Austin and the count fell to 380 by 1949. Growth began again in the 1960s, when the town was incorporated, and from 1980 through 1988 it was the fastest-growing community in Texas. For a seller, that recent boom means most houses were built in waves of new subdivisions, so builder and age matter more than street name when buyers compare.

sections.h2: What does a Texas tax bill mean for a Pflugerville seller?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so your bill comes from local units such as the county, a school district and the city. The county appraisal district values the house as of January 1, and the tax lien for that year attaches the same day.

Bills are mailed around October 1 and are delinquent if unpaid on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply then, and a collection attorney's fee of up to 20 percent can follow. Single-family homestead appraisal notices are mailed around April 1, and protests are generally due May 15.

  • School homestead exemption: $140,000 off a principal residence.
  • Owners 65 or older or disabled: $60,000 more, plus a school tax ceiling.
  • Appraisal cap: a homestead's appraised value rises no more than 10% a year.

Ask the Travis County tax office for a payoff, and let the title company split the current year's bill at closing.

sections.h2: Who records the deed for a Pflugerville sale?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the county clerk of the county where the land lies. For a Pflugerville house in Travis County that is the Travis County Clerk, and the seller signs before a notary or another officer who can take acknowledgments.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus records management, archive and technology fees. The title company confirms the total on your closing statement. General warranty and special warranty deeds are common in an ordinary sale.

If you are unsure which county holds your parcel, ask your title company before the deed is drafted, since a deed recorded in the wrong county causes delays.

sections.h2: What if the Pflugerville house has foreclosure or estate problems?
sections.html:
Each has a short clock. After a notice of default from a lender using power of sale, you can reinstate by paying the arrears within 20 days. A notice of sale follows at least 21 days before an auction on the first Tuesday of a month.

If a foreclosed sale leaves a gap, the lender has two years to sue for it, and surplus funds go to junior lienholders and then to the former owner. For inherited homes, a will is generally probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit may serve when the estate is $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

  • Missed payments: ask the servicer for a reinstatement figure in writing.
  • Back taxes: ask about an installment plan, which some collectors offer for up to 36 months on a homestead.
  • Inherited house: confirm who may sign before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How should I compare offers on a Pflugerville house?
sections.html:
Compare the money you keep and the date you get it. Take each offer, subtract commissions, repairs, holding costs, concessions and title charges, and set the totals side by side.

Ask whether the buyer will close on your date, whether an inspection can cancel the deal, who pays for the title policy and whether an earnest money deposit is required. If an owners' association governs the street, request its payoff or status letter early so it does not hold up closing.

faqs.q: Which county records a Pflugerville deed?
faqs.a: Travis County, for a house in northeastern Travis County where Pflugerville sits. Texas files deeds in the county where the land lies. Confirm your parcel's county with the title company.

faqs.q: When did Pflugerville start growing quickly?
faqs.a: In the 1980s. The Handbook of Texas calls it the fastest-growing community in the state from 1980 through 1988, and its population reached 16,335 by 2000.

faqs.q: When are Pflugerville property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. The Comptroller says a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1, and the penalty continues to grow monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Is there a deadline to protest my Pflugerville appraisal?
faqs.a: Generally May 15, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if that is later. The appraisal reflects value as of January 1, which can affect the tax split at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pflugerville house that is behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan is paid from your proceeds at closing. If a foreclosure notice has gone out, ask the servicer for the reinstatement amount and sale date, which falls on a first Tuesday.
